ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Sample Complexity of KernelSHAP Estimator
PROPOSAL: Analyze the sample complexity of KernelSHAP in terms of achieving a small Frobenius norm difference between the estimated and true Shapley value matrices, using techniques from empirical process theory, probabilistic analysis, and random matrix theory.
CONTROLS: Compare against LeverageSHAP, Random Sign Shapley, and no-regret Shapley on various real-world datasets (e.g., Fashion-MNIST, 20Newsgroups, IMDB) with synthetic and noise perturbations added.
COST: 6720
PREDICTION: We should be able to obtain non-asymptotic bounds on the trade-off between the estimation error, sample size, and dimension, specifically showing that KernelSHAP has a polynomial dependence on the dimension and sample size, but potentially weaker than the log-linear dependence of LeverageSHAP.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Dimensionality Scalability of LeverageSHAP and KernelSHAP
PROPOSAL: Investigate the dimensionality scalability of LeverageSHAP and KernelSHAP, by testing their performance on a large-scale synthetic dataset (generated using the Correlation lemma for high-dimensional Shapley) with varying dimensions (up to 1000 features) and controlled levels of feature redundancy and noise.
CONTROLS: Compare the robustness and speed-up of LeverageSHAP with KernelSHAP in high-dimensional settings, using baselines such as Random Sign Shapley and uniform sampling of Shapley subsets.
COST: 69120
PREDICTION: LeverageSHAP should demonstrate superior speed-up over KernelSHAP in high-dimensional settings, but at the cost of potentially higher bias, and we may observe feature redundancy reducing the gap between the performance of the two estimators.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Efficiency of Unique Subset Sums in KernelSHAP
PROPOSAL: Examine the efficiency of only considering unique subset sums in KernelSHAP, as opposed to all subset sums, by deriving theoretical bounds on the difference in estimated Shapley values and performing experiments on both real-world datasets (IMDB, 20Newsgroups) and synthetic datasets (including sparse and dense feature sets).
CONTROLS: Compare the efficiency and effectiveness of unique subset sums in KernelSHAP against using all subset sums, while varying the dimension and sparsity of the feature sets.
COST: 97920
PREDICTION: We should observe significant speedups from using unique subset sums, but potentially at the cost of a slight decrease in accuracy for complex datasets, and the bounds on the difference in estimated Shapley values may reveal the trade-offs between efficiency and effectivness.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Dimensionality Scalability of LeverageSHAP and KernelSHAP
PROPOSAL: Update the original proposal by incorporating dimension-specific kernels and weighted least squares, allowing for improved estimation of Shapley values in high-dimensional settings, and test the robustness of improved KernelSHAP against LeverageSHAP on large-scale real-world datasets (e.g., MS-COCO, WebVision).
CONTROLS: Compare LeverageSHAP, improved KernelSHAP, and Random Sign Shapley in terms of accuracy, speed, and robustness to noise and dimensionality.
COST: 104320
PREDICTION: Improved KernelSHAP should outperform both LeverageSHAP and Random Sign Shapley on large-scale datasets in terms of balance between accuracy and speed, but further analysis is required to determine whether this improvement comes at the cost of increased sample complexity.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Generalizing KernelSHAP to Robust Shapley Estimates
PROPOSAL: Develop a robust KernelSHAP variant by incorporating M-estimators, leverage scores, or similar techniques, to achieve more reliable Shapley estimates in the presence of noisy data or outliers, and provide theoretical guarantees on the robustness of the estimates.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the robust variant on real-world datasets with added noise or outliers (e.g., MNIST, CIFAR-10) and compare with the original KernelSHAP and LeverageSHAP in both clean and noisy settings.
COST: 180480
PREDICTION: We should be able to extend KernelSHAP to make it more robust to noisy data and outliers, and the M-estimator-based approach may offer improved robustness while still achieving fast convergence rates.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Unified Theoretical Framework for KernelSHAP Estimators
PROPOSAL: Develop a unified theoretical framework for KernelSHAP estimators, encompassing different sampling techniques, dimension-specific kernels, and robust M-estimators, to provide a coherent understanding of the relationships between these methods and derive bounds on their convergence rates and statistical guarantees.
CONTROLS: Derive theoretical bounds for various KernelSHAP extensions, including paired sampling, sampling without replacement, and robust estimators, and provide numerical experiments to validate the theoretical results on synthetic and real-world datasets.
COST: 373600
PREDICTION: We should be able to unify the theoretical foundations of KernelSHAP estimators and establish connections between different sampling methods, kernel functions, and robustification techniques, ultimately revealing the complex interplay between these factors and providing a roadmap for further research and improvements.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Efficient Implementation and Parallelization of KernelSHAP
PROPOSAL: Explore efficient implementation and parallelization strategies for KernelSHAP, including using GPU acceleration, parallel hashing, and blocking techniques, to significantly improve the computational speed and scalability of the estimator for large-scale applications, and benchmark the performance on various real-world datasets.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the parallelized implementation with the original sequential implementation, and examine the trade-offs between parallelization overhead, communication cost, and computational speedup.
COST: 817920
PREDICTION: We should be able to develop an efficient and parallel implementation of KernelSHAP that leverages modern computing hardware, resulting in orders-of-magnitude speed improvements for large-scale applications, and the parallelization strategies may also help to reduce the memory footprint and improve the overall robustness of the estimator.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Does Feature Dependence Matter in KernelSHAP Estimation?
PROPOSAL: Investigate the impact of feature dependence on KernelSHAP estimates, by designing experiments to test the robustness of KernelSHAP in settings with correlated, independent, and randomly dependent features, using both synthetic and real-world datasets (e.g., image classification, text analysis).
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of KernelSHAP on datasets with different feature dependencies, using metrics such as estimate accuracy, convergence rate, and stability.
COST: 1239424
PREDICTION: We should gain insight into the effect of feature dependence on KernelSHAP estimates, and, if feature dependence has a significant impact, we may need to adapt or extend KernelSHAP to handle realistic settings, potentially incorporating dependence modeling into the algorithm.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating KernelSHAP Across Machine Learning Tasks and Datasets
PROPOSAL: Conduct an extensive evaluation of KernelSHAP's performance across various machine learning tasks (regression, classification, clustering), datasets (uci-h Hint: a handpicked list of the UCI repository datasets ), and model architectures (traditional classification models, deep learning models), to assess its generalizability, robustness, and potential shortfalls.
CONTROLS: Compare KernelSHAP's performance on different tasks, datasets, and models, against baseline methods like LIME and SHAP, and examine the implications for different machine learning applications.
COST: 2786256
PREDICTION: We should gain a comprehensive understanding of KernelSHAP's strengths and weaknesses across different machine learning scenarios, and, if it shows robustness and generalizability, consider incorporating it into standard machine learning pipelines, alongside other model-agnostic explanations.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating the Fairness and Bias of KernelSHAP Explanations
PROPOSAL: Investigate the fairness and bias of KernelSHAP explanations, by analyzing whether the estimated feature importance values vary systematically across different groups, and whether these variations reflect or exacerbate existing biases in the data, using both theoretical framework and real-world case studies.
CONTROLS: Compare the fairness and bias of KernelSHAP explanations with other model-agnostic explanation methods, and examine the potential harm or unfairness introduced by biased explanations.
COST: 7045632
PREDICTION: We should be able to identify and praise fair and unbiased explanations that provide meaningful insights, and further develop and test fairness-aware variants of KernelSHAP to reduce its bias and increase its trustworthiness.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Long-Range Temporal Dynamics in MMLMs for Change Understanding
PROPOSAL: We will modify a multimodal large language model (MMLM) to incorporate a new temporal awareness module that enables long-range temporal reasoning and dynamic change understanding through a graph-structured knowledge retrieval and fusion mechanism. This module will process the sequence of images and their corresponding captions, learn temporal relationships between events and changes, and induce a structural causal model to describe the drivers of change. We will employ a publicly available MMLM framework (e.g., CLIP orALIGN) as the base model and integrate the new temporal awareness module as a conditional transformer.
CONTROLS: We will compare against the original MMLM and a variant that adds a simple timestamp interaction module for basic temporal awareness.
COST: 4500
PREDICTION: This revised MMLM will significantly outperform the baselines in capturing long-range temporal dynamics and accurately describing dynamic changes in the test dataset. However, its ability to accurately reason about causality and the underlying drivers of change might be limited, and it may fail to generalize to previously unseen change patterns.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating Temporal Consistency in Future Satellite Image Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We propose a new evaluation metric, TS-CIDE (Temporal Scene Consistency and Inconsistency Descriptor Estimator), to measure the temporal consistency of forecasted images with historical satellite image trends. TS-CIDE combines a concise and numerical descriptor of the scene consistency (e.g., directional change in land use) with an inconsistency term that quantifies deviations from observed historical patterns. We will use TS-CIDE to evaluate and compare the performance of three state-of-the-art image forecasting methods (e.g., SAGAN, StarGANv2, and a popular diffusion model) on a subset of the targeted satellite image datasets.
CONTROLS: Our proposed metric will be compared against the standard image-quality metrics (e.g., PSNR and SSIM) for satellite images.
COST: 9000
PREDICTION: TS-CIDE will effectively distinguish between temporally consistent and inconsistent future scene forecasts, and the top-performing model according to TS-CIDE may differ from the model with the highest image-quality metrics. However, as TS-CIDE is a novel metric, its reliability and real-world applicability might be questioned.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Enhancing Long-Range Temporal Understanding for Joint Change Description and Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We propose an extension of the MMLM with long-range temporal dynamics (proposal 1) that integrates a generative forecasting module to predict future scene states. This module will be conditioned on the enhanced MMLM's dynamic change understanding and temporal awareness, ensuring that forecasted changes are a logical continuation of observed historical trends. We will dynamically infer the sequence length to be predicted based on the model's confidence in forecasting future changes.
CONTROLS: We will compare this joint model against the MMLM with long-range temporal dynamics for change understanding (proposal 1), a state-of-the-art image forecasting model, and a model that combines a change description method with a separate image forecasting component.
COST: 18000
PREDICTION: This enhanced MMLM will outperform the baselines in both change description and forecasting tasks, particularly for longer-term predictions, as it leverages its deep understanding of past changes to generate coherent future scenarios. However, if the model struggles to capture infrequently observed patterns or abrupt changes, its performance might degrade significantly.

NUMBER: 3
TITLE: Enhancing Long-Range Temporal Understanding for Joint Change Description and Forecasting (Revised)
PROPOSAL: We revise the joint model to incorporate an attention-based temporal sparse convolutional network for scene change forecasting. This module will be designed to focus on critical areas of the historical scene changes and adaptively increase the prediction capacity for longer-term forecasting. Additionally, we will develop a hierarchical knowledge retrieval mechanism that captures both high-level semantic change patterns and low-level spatial details from the historical data to further improve the forecasting accuracy.
CONTROLS: The revised model will be compared against the same baselines as before.
COST: 27000
PREDICTION: The revised joint model will achieve improved performance in forecasting tasks, especially for longer-term predictions and scenarios with intricate changes. ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Ablation Study for the Hierarchical Knowledge Retrieval Mechanism
PROPOSAL: We perform an ablation study to investigate the impact of the hierarchical knowledge retrieval mechanism on the revised joint model's performance. We will examine two ablated versions: one without the hierarchical knowledge retrieval mechanism, and another with only the high-level semantic pattern retrieval module. By comparing the results, we can elucidate the importance and potential benefits of the proposed mechanism in forecasting accuracy and scene change understanding.
CONTROLS: We will compare the ablated models against the revised joint model (proposal 3), the original MMLM with long-range temporal dynamics, and a state-of-the-art image forecasting model.
COST: 10800
PREDICTION: The ablation study will demonstrate that the hierarchical knowledge retrieval mechanism contributes significantly to the forecasting accuracy, and removing it will lead to decreased performance. However, the exact impact might depend on the complexity of the scene changes and the availability of historical data for the retrieval mechanism to learn from.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Experiments on Real-World Satellite Image Time Series
PROPOSAL: We will evaluate the revised joint model (proposal 3) and the ablated versions from the ablation study (proposal 4) on three real-world satellite image time series datasets (e.g., LSHTM's Change Detection dataset, Terra-Aqua dataset, and EROS dataset) using a subset of the datasets' images. We will assess their performance in change description and forecasting tasks, comparing against state-of-the-art methods used in the respective datasets.
CONTROLS: We will compare the results of the revised joint model and the ablated versions against state-of-the-art methods for each dataset, as well as record the baseline performance of the original MMLM with long-range temporal dynamics and a state-of-the-art image forecasting model.
COST: 16200
PREDICTION: The revised joint model will achieve state-of-the-art performance on the real-world datasets, and the ablated versions will demonstrate the significant impact of the hierarchical knowledge retrieval mechanism on the forecasting accuracy. However, the results might be sensitive to the quality and characteristics of the real-world data used in the experiments.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Impact of Scene Complexity on Model Performance
PROPOSAL: We will analyze the effect of scene complexity on the performance of the revised joint model (proposal 3) and the ablated versions from the ablation study (proposal 4) using the results from the real-world satellite image time series experiments (proposal 5). We will examine how different scene complexities (e.g., urban, rural, coastal areas) affect the model's ability to accurately describe changes and forecast future scenes.
CONTROLS: We will perform statistical analysis on the experiment results to quantify the impact of scene complexity on model performance.
COST: 13500
PREDICTION: The study will reveal that scene complexity significantly influences the performance of the revised joint model and the ablated versions, with the hierarchical knowledge retrieval mechanism showing improved performance for more complex scenes. However, the relationship between scene complexity and model performance might be influenced by other factors, such as the availability of historical data and the quality of the satellite images.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Temporal-Spatial Coherence for Improved Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We propose a new temporal-spatial coherence loss function to encourage the forecasted scenes to maintain both temporal consistency (as evaluated in proposal 2) and spatial coherence with the historical scenes. The loss function will be integrated into the revised joint model (proposal 3) and tested on the real-world satellite image time series datasets.
CONTROLS: We will compare the results of the revised joint model with the temporal-spatial coherence loss function against the original revised joint model and the ablated versions from the ablation study.
COST: 19800
PREDICTION: The introduction of the temporal-spatial coherence loss function will significantly improve the forecasting accuracy of the revised joint model, particularly for scenes with intricate spatial structures and changes. However, the additional complexity might make the training process more computationally intensive and sensitive to hyperparameter tuning.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Presentation of the Model as a Unified Tool for Change Understanding and Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We propose to develop an end-to-end, unified framework that combines the MMLM with long-range temporal dynamics (proposal 1), the revised joint model for change description and forecasting (proposal 3), and the temporal-spatial coherence loss function (proposal 7) into a single tool for both understanding change in satellite image time series and forecasting future scenes. This unified framework will enable users to easily toggle between change description and forecasting tasks, and to explore the complex relationships between scene changes and future predictions.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of the unified framework against the individual components and state-of-the-art baselines for both tasks.
COST: 45000
PREDICTION: The unified framework will enable users to easily and effectively utilize the MMLM's capabilities for change understanding and forecasting, and will demonstrate improved performance and usability compared to existing tools and methods. However, integrating the components into a single framework might require additional computational resources and tuning of hyperparameters for optimal performance.
